jobs.title: Lot C, ii
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 21, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE GUARD — middle-aged man in a dark campus security windbreaker and cap, clipboard, standing bent slightly as if to a car window. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Wednesday. The guard explains the lots. A is for faculty. B is for students who arrive early. C is for cowards. Wood parks in C. Panel 1: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a security guard in a navy windbreaker bent to a rusted small car's window with a clipboard in the rain, a young man inside (in this panel: THE GUARD, WOOD). Guard says "A is faculty. B is early. C is —". Wood says "Cowards. You said.". Panel 2: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a security guard's face under a cap, philosophical (in this panel: THE GUARD). Guard says "C is for people who could've been in B.". Panel 3: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man in a car looking up a hill at a half-empty parking lot closer to a building, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man sitting in a parked car in the far lot as a guard walks away satisfied (in this panel: WOOD, THE GUARD). Wood says "I'm comfortable here.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17.
